## Corrected callouts · Visual Design Reviewer

**Decision — APPROVE.** The native summary, trailing arrow and keyboard outline clearly identify which panels open. Search now shows the matched text inside a folded panel, and the complete focus outline around the shared-mailbox link is visible.

- **Builds and evidence.** I inspected the accepted preview on port 47832 and corrected preview on 47834 in fresh Chromium sessions at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900, in both light and pure-black dark themes. I examined the twelve corrected paired sheets for disclosures, static callouts, surroundings and forced colors against the live site.
- **Pages and states.** I inspected all eleven callouts in Azure documentation, Dynamic Group for Shared Mailboxes, Microsoft Defender SmartScreen, WinGet, Azure Machine Configuration and the Active Directory project article. I toggled each of the five disclosures with the pointer, tabbed to its summary, then pressed Space. I also inspected Home, the 56-item Blog listing, opened and closed Explorer and Search, inspected the adjacent Azure PowerShell fence, and opened and dismissed the global graph in tablet light and desktop dark. The mobile Home graph remained hidden. Under reduced motion the disclosure and icon reported zero-duration transitions.
- **Search.** I selected the real WinGet result from the Blog search for both phrases on both builds at every size and theme. In the corrected build “Legacy Applications” highlights the title on the closed panel. “employee requires older version” opens the panel and highlights the phrase within its paragraph. Both marks land around the middle of the visible viewport, between 435 and 444 CSS pixels from the top. In the baseline the body result reached the panel with its content still folded.
- **Alignment, type and themes.** Title and status icon share a stable left alignment. The right-facing or downward arrow occupies a consistent position across different title lengths. Static note and tip panels retain their blue and green treatments. Source Serif 4 at weights 600 and 425 preserves title and body hierarchy. The five disclosures have the same resting heights as the baseline at all widths. Their summaries measure 58, 60 and 61 CSS pixels. Above and below the Azure callout, the reading column, section heading, TX-02 code and side navigation retain their alignment and spacing.
- **Wrapped link and focus.** In the Shared Mailboxes panel the 2px keyboard ring with its 3px offset follows the entire wrapped link. Phone captures in light and dark forced colors show the left segment of the final line of “How to add a shared mailbox in Outlook” completely enclosed. That segment is clipped on the accepted build. The summary's own focus ring remains legible in both standard themes.
- **Maintainability and severity.** Styling the native summary inside the existing callout blockquote reuses the original panel geometry and theme tokens. The flow-root body contains paragraph margins and gives link outlines space. I found no critical, material or minor visual regression, and have no outstanding changes to request.

# Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer, corrected candidate

**APPROVE.** The corrected WinGet search result exposes the matched passage while keeping keyboard focus on Search. The wrapped Outlook link now has a complete focus outline. I found no outstanding accessibility or responsive defect in this change.

**Pages and evidence.** I opened the accepted build on port 47832 and the corrected build on port 47834, inspected all 12 corrected paired sheets, and tested all 11 callouts on the six published articles. These included Azure Documentation, Shared Mailboxes, SmartScreen, WinGet, Azure Machine Configuration and the Active Directory project. I tested Chromium and Playwright WebKit at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels in light and pure-black dark.

**Search.** I opened the visible Search control in the Blog listing, entered each query and clicked the actual “Automatically Update Apps through Intune (WinGet)” result. Searching “Legacy Applications” highlighted the title in view with the panel closed. Searching “employee requires older version” expanded the panel and displayed the highlighted body phrase. The focus event recorder showed no transfer to either the disclosure or its highlight. The Search button retained focus. Both engines passed both queries at all three widths under reduced motion. WebKit also passed the phone and desktop cases with normal motion.

**Keyboard, touch and assistive technology.** Tab reaches the named summary. Enter and Space toggle its native state, and phone taps do the same. Chromium's accessibility tree reported the expanded and collapsed values. The Outlook link disappeared from both keyboard traversal and the accessibility tree when collapsed, then returned as the next tab stop when reopened. WebKit confirmed this sequence. On direct load, five disclosures had their authored states and six static panels had no disclosure control. With JavaScript disabled, Enter, Space and touch still operated WinGet in both engines.

**Visibility and readability.** On mobile, matched forced-color images show the left edge of the Outlook link outline now extends beyond the wrapped paragraph into the panel padding. Both the light and dark palettes show that 2px outline and the summary's inset focus outline. The title row measured 58–61px tall. Tip title contrast measured 5.24:1 in light and 11.57:1 in dark, body text 16.56:1 and 18.23:1, and the fold arrow 3.61:1 and 7.60:1. Source Serif 4 and TX-02 retain their respective reading and code roles. All 11 panel dimensions matched their accepted counterparts across the six Chromium viewport and theme combinations. At actual Chromium tab zoom of 200% and 400%, the expanded WinGet disclosure, title and body fit 640px and 320px layout viewports with zero horizontal overflow.

**Surroundings and maintainability.** Home search remained keyboard-operable and returned focus on Escape. Mobile Explorer opened. Blog listing navigation reached Azure Machine Configuration and its adjacent code by SPA. Global Graph opened on the tablet and desktop and returned focus on Escape. Reduced motion hid the graph, disabled smooth scrolling, and removed transitions from the disclosure body, title and arrow. The outer Quartz blockquote remains available to search, native details owns disclosure state, and the body formatting rule permits link focus outlines to paint into the panel padding. The search observer uses the existing navigation cleanup signal and acts only on matched disclosure bodies.

**Severity and limits.** No outstanding critical, material or minor issue in the reviewed callouts. The initial wrapped-outline defect is resolved. No discretionary changes requested. Accessibility-tree and keyboard checks used browser automation. Physical screen-reader and device testing were outside this review.

Independent results and focus screenshots are in /tmp/quartz-callout-pass/access-final. Source records are access-chromium.json, access-webkit.json, access-zoom-ui.json, verified-checked-search-chromium.json, verified-checked-search-webkit.json, verified-motion-search-webkit.json, nojstest.json and link.json. The matched focus images are focused-author-47832-light.png, focused-author-47834-light.png and their dark counterparts.

# Corrected CSS and Quartz V5 review

**APPROVE.** Both search journeys that failed the first review now land on the intended content. The corrected stylesheet and transformer preserve the article layout and native disclosure behavior.

## Evidence from the corrected preview

- Compared the runnable baseline on port 47832 and the corrected build on 47834 in Chromium at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in light and pure-black dark modes. Reviewed the paired disclosure, fixed note, forced-color and full-page sheets at every width, and both additional search comparison sheets. Opened Home, the Blog archive, Azure Machine Configuration, WinGet, Azure documentation and Shared Mailboxes. Exercised Explorer, search, article navigation, repeat renders, the adjacent code sample and the global graph. The global graph opened to a canvas at 1440 in both builds and Escape restored its launcher focus. [Independent viewport measurements](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-matrix2.json)
- From the archive, selecting the WinGet result for “Legacy Applications” highlights the visible summary while the panel stays closed. For “employee requires older version” it opens the panel and brings its highlighted body text into view. The control search for “Microsoft Intune Rollout” lands on the ordinary heading and leaves the panel closed. Selecting the Shared Mailboxes result for “manual actions” reaches its already-open callout. [Corrected search measurements](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-search2-47834.json) · [Baseline search measurements](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-search2-47832.json)
- Using a nested callout fixture in the actual WinGet article and Quartz's own Search matching path, a nested title match opened the enclosing panel and left the matched summary closed. A body match opened both ancestors. Instrumenting the browser's MutationObserver showed one active callout observer watching both relevant bodies after three renders. On SPA navigation to the archive, the observer count dropped to zero. An ordinary content mutation, dismissal of search with Escape and a fresh ordinary WinGet visit all preserved the expected closed state. Escape restored focus to the search launcher.
- The native summary accepted Enter and Space in all six width/theme combinations, with a solid keyboard outline at every width. On the actual Shared Mailboxes page with JavaScript disabled, Chromium exposed the labeled DisclosureTriangle and reported expanded true, false, true through keyboard toggles. The body link disappeared from the closed accessibility tree and returned on re-opening. Tab skipped that link when closed and reached it when open with the site's scripts enabled. [Script-free accessibility probe](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-native.cjs)

## CSS and build integration

- The outer callout retains its original blockquote, class names for appearance, metadata and margins. The native details inside restores Search's blockquote match target without adding a second state controller. Installed OFM only binds its click listener to the state class removed by the build transformer. The existing navigation lifecycle disconnects the callout search observer on render or navigation. Its observation is limited to the contents of actual article disclosures and acts on inserted Search markers.
- CSS under `.callout > details` targets the immediate summary, arrow and content. Flow-root contains margins and lets a wrapped focus outline paint. The unchanged parent blockquote owns column and heading spacing. Measured outer widths on the Azure callout were 354.9, 656.5 and 688px. Title rows were 58, 60 and 61px. Open and closed panel geometry, static-note geometry and article wrapping matched the baseline at all widths. Title/prose retained Source Serif 4, Explorer retained SN Pro and adjacent fenced code retained TX-02. The masked arrows used system black or white in forced colors. The paired screenshots show the expected inline-end arrow and fresh focus outline in both themes.
- The two focused HAST tests passed independently. They cover nested states, title links and emphasis, preservation of attributes and body nodes, unchanged static notes, empty folds and reapplication. The correction introduces no dependency.

**Defects and severity.** The two demonstrated material failures from the first cycle are resolved. No new material or critical regression was found in this review.

# Design Director — corrected callout disclosures

**APPROVE.** The Visual Design, Responsive and Accessibility, and CSS and Quartz V5 reviewers each independently approved the corrected build. I reproduced both Search failures on the first candidate and verified both fixes on the corrected live site. The corrected version resolves the material regressions and the minor wrapped-link focus defect from the first review.

From the Blog listing in Chrome at 900 × 900, I selected the WinGet result for “Legacy Applications.” The title appeared in view with a visible highlight and the disclosure stayed closed. Selecting the same result for “employee requires older version” expanded the disclosure and displayed the highlighted phrase. Chrome, Brave and Firefox also recorded visible title and body marks at the phone and desktop sizes. The CSS reviewer confirmed that the surrounding headings and nested disclosures keep their correct states after Search, repeated renders and navigation. [Title selection](revised-director-search-47834-Legacy.json) · [Body selection](revised-director-search-47834-employee.json)

On Shared Mailboxes, I compared both builds at 390, 900 and 1440px. The corrected summary closed by pointer, kept the hidden Outlook link out of focus and the accessibility tree, and reopened with Space. Tab then reached the link. Phone controls also worked with page JavaScript disabled. The black page, serif reading type and trailing chevron remain legible in the dark theme. My 390px forced-color capture shows a continuous focus outline around the wrapped link. Reviewers verified matching panel geometry, static callouts, adjacent code, zoom up to 400%, reduced motion and the surrounding site navigation. [Native interaction observations](revised-director-browser.json) · [Wrapped link at 390px](revised-director-mobile.png)

Quartz Search has an inherited limitation for phrases that start or end inside inline code. On both baseline and corrected WinGet, “WinGet with --all” and “--all parameter will” bring the folded panel into view without generating a highlight. Both builds reproduce this behavior. The corrected version opens for “WinGet with --all parameter,” where Quartz generates a body match. This finding limits the claim to generated body highlights and does not block acceptance of the disclosure change. [Inline-code selection](revised-director-rich-search-47834-WinGet%2520with%2520--all.json)

The corrected build emitted 913 files. All 166 unit tests passed, alongside formatting and whitespace checks. Across 252 routes, heading IDs, link destinations, callout copy, author-specified states and font assets matched. The separate repository type check retains its two pre-existing declaration errors for micromorph and remark-parse/lib. No material regression remains within the change reviewed.
